To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
citrate, calcium and modest reductions of kidney function alter utilization and toxicity of orally administered aluminum.
modest reductions in kidney functions and dietary citrate increase the utilization of trace elements.
dietary citrate and modest reductions in renal function can increase aluminum retention in tissues of rats fed aluminum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of dietary citrate, calcium and modest changes in renal function in the absorption and retention of aluminum, zinc, copper, iron and calcium in rats.
the effects of dietary factors on the utilization of aluminum in rats.
the role of citrate and kidney disease in the pathogenesis of the dialysis encephalopathy syndrome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of dietary calcium, citrate and kidney disease on aluminum retention is dependent on the dose of aluminum, the route of administration, the species and the duration of exposure.
aluminum, zinc and calcium are affected by citrate and kidney disease in the rat.
dietary citrate and kidney dysfunction can increase tissue aluminum concentrations, whereas dietary calcium and kidney function can decrease tissue aluminum concentrations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the solubility and absorption of trace minerals in the gut is affected by the dietary intake of citrate and by the kidney's ability to clear these metals from the blood.
the kidney plays a central role in the metabolism of many metals, and that dietary components such as citrate and calcium can affect the utilization of metals by the kidneys and other tissues.
aluminum is a relatively non-toxic element, and that aluminum is not an essential element.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aluminum is poorly absorbed and poorly retained in the body when ingested in food.
dietary citrate and kidney disease can affect the utilization of aluminum, zinc and other trace minerals.
the kidney plays an important role in determining the amount of aluminum that is retained in bone.
